title: Maximize Total Cost of Alternating Subarrays
summary: Given an integer array nums, define the cost of a subarray as the alternating sum of its elements.
statement: Given an integer array nums, define the cost of a subarray as the alternating sum of its elements. The goal is to split nums into subarrays to maximize the total cost, where the total cost is the sum of individual subarray costs. Each element must be in exactly one subarray. The task is to find the maximum total cost achievable by optimally splitting the array.
constraints: nums is a nonempty integer array.
Split it into nonempty contiguous parts; a part costs first-second+third-fourth and so on.
Maximize the sum of all part costs while using every element exactly once.
hints: At each position retain the best total when the current element receives a plus or minus sign within its part.
A plus may begin a new part after either state; a minus can only continue after a plus.
These are the only legal roles for the next element, so induction preserves the best cost for both possible ending signs.
editorial: These are the only legal roles for the next element, so induction preserves the best cost for both possible ending signs.

tests.explanation: Keeping 1,-2,3 together costs six and starting a new part at four gives total ten.
The only part contains -5, so the maximum total is -5.
